answers.text: Instruction: always give exactly three lines, in this order - delivery date, item and quantity, any change from the original order - using the same wording each time. If one of the three isn't mentioned in the email, write 'not stated' for that line rather than leaving it out. That's the whole trick - same three lines, every time.
The memo should list date, amount, category, submitter in that order, then a total of all the amounts at the end.
Something's off with the dates in that email - the delivery date given doesn't actually match the three-day gap they mention from the call.
62 deliveries against 54 last week is close enough to the 15% they say. The on-time rate looks off though - 3 late out of 62 should be around 95%, not 97%.

I'd sign off Output 2 - it shows the actual sales and returns figures behind the 4.1%, not just the answer. Output 1 might well be correct, but there's no way to check it without re-running the numbers yourself, since it doesn't show where 4.1% came from.
I'd send Reply 2, since it has the order and credit reference numbers. Reply 1 doesn't say which order this even is, so there's nothing to check the 10% credit against.

The pricing and discount terms need care before anything goes into an unvetted tool, and the confidentiality clause is the same story since it names both companies directly - I'd treat both of those as no-go without checking first.
Before sending the report out, I'd check the delivery and on-time numbers against the system directly rather than trusting the draft as it is.
The first step, reading the order email and pulling the details, is the one I'd watch most, since everything after depends on getting that right.
